purpose: possession is not accompaniment; a physically held object's location after its holder moves is unsupported_transport_dependency, never a validated stale position
text: Tom is a person. Tom is in the hall. The key is in the hall. Tom holds the key. Tom can walk from the hall to the garden.

units.text: Tom is a person. Tom is in the hall.
The key is in the hall.
units.note: a place, so located_at, not container in (A2.2)

must_have.note: the stated-endpoint path: the rule's conditions, located_at, differ and the hook; no connected literal

units.note: walk maps to the standard means foot

queries.text: How can the key get to the garden?

expect.evidence: a held object (S3) with a tracked location (S2) whose holder can move (S4), and a query about the object's location: the library lacks the co-movement transition. Not not_found, which would hide the missing transition.

queries.text: After Tom walks to the garden, is the key in the hall?

expect.evidence: the stale position located_at(key,hall) at W0+1 would be validated at 0.99 by frame_located_at; the route must not answer Yes

queries.text: After Tom walks to the garden, is Tom in the garden?

expect.evidence: the query does not depend on the key's location; the dependency check is per query, not per source. S4's permission with its scoped route; eff_move_at.

variants.text: Tom is a person. Tom is in the hall. The key is in the hall. Tom has the key. Tom can walk from the hall to the garden.

expect.evidence: possession alone does not imply physical accompaniment (A2.2); no action moves the key; the transport diagnostic applies to a held object only
the key's location persists; nothing in the source says the key travels

queries.text: After Tom walks to the garden, does Tom have the key?

candidates.reason: Q1/Q2: the replayed state after step 1 contains a held object whose holder moved; the replay reports the uncovered transport dependency rather than validating the stale key location (A5.1 not_checked)

support.compile: supported; the transport dependency is a query-time diagnostic

explain: Fable addenda point 10 (accompaniment) with Astra's remedy. The base text has all three ingredients: a tracked key location, holding, and a holder move. Q1 and Q2 concern the key and are diagnosed; Q3 concerns Tom only and is answered. The possession_only variant shows the have/holding distinction: with have there is no transport claim, so the key staying in the hall is the correct reading and Q2 is Yes.
notes: holding(Tom,key) uses the same fluent the blocks model uses for a hand; the relation has actor and object slots and handhood constrains only the library's default permission, not every holding fact (REVIEW.md disposition 6). The library's take/put_on laws do not apply to Tom (no isa hand), which is why no plan can move the key either way.
